title: Reinstatement Deposit Floors and Running Disability Compensation Awards — Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery
content:
On a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery**, the floor under a reinstatement deposit depends on how recently the cancelled plan was approved and on whether the debtor holds a running **Disability Compensation** award.

**Rule.** When the cancelled plan was approved no more than the reinstatement window of 6 whole months ago and the debtor holds a running Disability Compensation award, the counted installments multiplied by their value are raised to at least the compensation deposit floor of 450.00 USD. When the plan was approved within that window and the debtor holds no running Disability Compensation award, they are raised to at least the other deposit floor of 200.00 USD. When the plan was approved more than 6 whole months ago, no floor under this rule applies.

**Reading the records.** The approval is the latest repayment plan decision on the debt; its age is counted in whole calendar months from the approval date to the day of the payment. Whether the award is running is read from the status of the debtor's Disability Compensation award.

| Whole months since approval | Running Disability Compensation award | Deposit floor |
|---|---|---|
| 6 or fewer | Yes | 450.00 USD |
| 6 or fewer | No | 200.00 USD |
| 7 or more | Either | No floor under this rule |

**Hypothetical cases.**

- Approved 4 whole months ago, running compensation award, counted installments worth 174.80 USD: raised to 450.00 USD.
- Approved exactly 6 whole months ago, no running award, installments worth 310.00 USD: already above 200.00 USD, so 310.00 USD stands.
- Approved 7 whole months ago: this rule sets no floor.
